title: 📱 The "Jolla" phone returns with Linux: a replaceable battery and privacy without Google!
body: 📱 The "Jolla" phone returns with Linux: a replaceable battery and privacy without Google!

Finnish company Jolla has opened pre-orders for its new phone, the "Jolla Phone", a privacy-focused handset running Sailfish OS 5, built on Linux, instead of Android and Google services. It costs 499 euros, with a refundable booking deposit of 99 euros, delivery expected in mid-2026, and sales planned for the European Union, Britain, Norway, and Switzerland.

The phone carries a 6.36-inch AMOLED screen, a MediaTek processor supporting 5G that the company has not yet specified, 12 GB of memory, 256 GB of storage, and a dual 50-megapixel rear camera. Its standout feature is a 5,500 mAh battery the user can replace themselves, at a time when most batteries are glued inside the phone and can only be replaced at repair centres.

The whole idea is that the phone does not rely on a Google account or its services: the Sailfish system gives the user greater control over their data, and offers an alternative for anyone who wants a phone that works without sending every step to a big company. But that also means popular Android apps may not work on it in the same way, and the company is small compared with the phone giants.

Simply put: a phone that recalls the days when the battery could be swapped in seconds, and a system that does not send your data to Google; would you accept giving up some apps in exchange for more privacy and a battery you can replace yourself?
